To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

psychiatric patients can present with symptoms that are not psychiatric in nature, that medical patients can present with psychiatric symptoms and that psychiatric patients can have more than one diagnosis, both psychiatric and medical, at the same time.

(1) psychiatric patients may have medical illnesses that present with psychiatric symptoms, (2) medical patients may have psychiatric illnesses presenting with medical symptoms, and (3) psychiatric patients may also have medical illnesses.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following issues: 1) the psychiatric presentations of medical illnesses, 2) the medical presentations of psychiatric illnesses, and 3) the presence of psychiatric illnesses in the presence of a medical illness.
the psychiatric manifestations of medical illnesses and the psychiatric presentations of medical illnesses, and their differential diagnostic considerations.
how to make a correct psychiatric or medical diagnosis when the symptoms are ambiguous and how to avoid a misdiagnosis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

a medical illness may present with symptoms pointing to a psychiatric diagnosis, a psychiatric illness may present with a medical diagnostic symptomatology, and a psychiatric patient may have more than 1 psychiatric and/or medical diagnosis.
a psychiatric diagnosis is not a final diagnosis, but a working diagnosis that must be re-evaluated with each patient visit.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the psychiatrist must be aware of the differential psychiatric diagnosis and at the same time be aware of the psychiatric manifestations of medical illnesses.
the psychiatric diagnosis should be made first, and then a medical diagnosis secondarily.
psychiatric patients may present with a variety of symptoms that are not necessarily psychiatric.
The main takeaway from our work is that
psychiatric and medical illnesses may present similarly and it is incumbent on the physician to be aware of this and not make a hasty psychiatric diagnosis.
the psychiatrist needs to be aware of medical illnesses that can present with psychiatric symptoms, and that psychiatric illnesses can present with medical symptoms.
